context_of_use: Simple synthetic engineering comparison of R-peak and RR robustness across independent clean and continuous-noise SNR cases.

limitations: Synthetic signals do not establish clinical sensitivity, specificity, population generalization, or diagnostic safety.
A PASS applies only to the exact package, evidence level, verifier, algorithm build, submission, and hashes recorded in the evidence bundle.
The cited sources inform design and interpretation; none directly specifies the complete Synsigra case matrix and numeric gate set.
evidence_basis.numeric_threshold_basis: Pack-author pre-specified engineering gates selected for discrimination, regression stability, and the exact deterministic protocol; no numeric gate is copied from a cited standard or study.
evidence_basis.rationale: Independent continuous-noise cases expose the performance curve from clean through -11 dB without pooling. Values below -6 dB and the exact F1/RR gates intentionally extend beyond the official NSTDB ladder and remain Synsigra engineering criteria.

sources.citation: Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation. Testing and reporting performance results of cardiac rhythm and ST segment measurement algorithms. 2012, reaffirmed 2020.
sources.limitation: The public scope page does not supply transferable Synsigra PASS/FAIL values, and Synsigra does not claim EC57 conformity.

evidence_boundary: Synthetic engineering QA evidence for R-peak detection and beat-to-beat RR measurement; not diagnosis, clinical validation, or regulatory qualification.

evidence_profile.description: A demanding engineering gate for high-performing implementations and additional regression headroom. It is not clinical evidence.
evidence_profile.threshold_adjustment: Relative to Level 2: minimum gates are increased by 0.05 (ceiling 1); maximum error gates are multiplied by 0.75.

truth_policy.artifact_overlap: Noise and artifacts remain scoreable because each complete case is the unit of evaluation.
truth_policy.boundary: Only construction events crossing the record boundary are excluded; no blanket edge window is used.
truth_policy.event_reporting_basis: R-peak TP, FP, FN, sensitivity and positive predictive value use Synsigra's +/-50 ms closest-event window. This is deliberately tighter than the default 150 ms WFDB bxb window; Synsigra does not claim bxb identity or EC57 conformity.
truth_policy.event_scoreability: Complete in-record constructed QRS events are scoreable; every exclusion is reported.
truth_policy.literature_context: Thresholds are pre-specified for this exact deterministic synthetic protocol, informed by PhysioNet MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database and peer-reviewed noisy-QRS benchmarks; SNR labels are not directly interchangeable across protocols.
truth_policy.rr_association: Valid RR intervals are anchored by their ending R-peak time and associated when their overlap covers more than half of the shorter interval. FP splits and FN merges create local comparison pairs; unique interval coverage cannot exceed 100%.
truth_policy.rr_definition: Difference between consecutive scoreable construction R-peak times; the first beat has no in-record RR value.
truth_policy.rr_statistics_boundary: RR tolerance percentage, MAE and median are pre-specified case gates. P95 remains a visible diagnostic because split/merge outliers make it unsuitable as the primary ladder gate. These are Synsigra engineering limits, not ANSI/AAMI EC57 or IEC conformity claims.
truth_policy.scope: R-peak event and RR measurement files are required; signal quality, HRV, classification, and delineation are outside the evidence matrix.
